question: to the Commission Marc Botenga (The Left) Subject:

The Commission states that the framework governing Horizon Europe cooperation with Israeli and Russian entities differs, inter alia, because, unlike Russia, Israel has an association agreement with the EU1. The 2008 Protocol to the 1995 Euro-Mediterranean Association Agreement2 allows Israel to participate in Community programmes open to it3. However, the 2022 agreement on the participation of Israel in Horizon Europe between the EU represented by the Commission, and Israel, also provides that either party may terminate the agreement at any time by written notification4. A 2017 legal opinion by the Director-General of the Commission’s Legal Service found that the EU was legally entitled to suspend research cooperation with Israel5. A 2025 formal review of Israel’s compliance with the 1995 agreement also confirmed indications that Israel had breached Article 2 thereof. 1.
What prevents the Commission from invoking the termination clause in Article 9.4 of the 2022 agreement on the participation of Israel in Horizon Europe?

Does the Commission consider that within this framework it has the competence to adopt interim measures such as the suspension of new grant agreements and payment flows, analogous to those applied to Russian entities in March 2022?
If not, which legal provision explains why such measures could be applied to Russian entities but not to Israeli entities?
